request.spec:
Change how a new invoice's due date is set. Instead of 30 days after it is issued, make it due
on the last day of the month after the month it was issued in: issued 2026-01-31, due
2026-02-28; issued in December, due at the end of January.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Change how a new invoice's due date is set. Instead of 30 days after it is issued, make it due
on the last day of the month after the month it was issued in: issued 2026-01-31, due
2026-02-28; issued in December, due at the end of January.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
New invoices are now due on the last day of the month after the month they're issued in, and both tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The fix is all on the server, in `InvoiceService.java`:
- I removed the 30-day payment-terms constant.
- A new `dueDateFor(issued)` method moves the issue date forward one month and returns the last day of that month. So 2026-01-31 gives 2026-02-28, and December gives 31 January of the next year.

I also updated the comment on `newDraft` in the front-end `invoice.service.ts` to describe the new rule.

Invoices that already exist keep the due date they have, and no data or schema changes were needed.
